newsitem.title: IRAQ: Rebel Kurds vow to resist Turkish security zone.
newsitem.headline: Rebel Kurds vow to resist Turkish security zone.

text.p: A Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebel commander, hunkered down inside the boundaries of Turkey's planned security zone, said on Saturday that his men were prepared to resist any incursion by Turkish forces.
"If the Turks come we will launch a guerrilla war against them," said the 28-year-old unit commander, who gave his name only as Dostvan.

"We actually want them to come, so we can deal them a heavy blow and defeat them," he told reporters near Banek, 30 km (20 miles) northeast of the main Iraqi border town of Zakho. His escort stood by with Kalashnikov rifles at the ready.
Ankara has said it was preparing to create a security zone just across the Iraqi border, five to 10 km (three to six miles) deep, to root out PKK bases used to attack Turkish targets.
The United States has given conditional approval to the plan, but a number of other countries, among them France and Russia, have protested against the plan.

Dostvan said Ankara was just as interested in seizing Iraqi territory as defeating the PKK, which has been waging a bloody insurgency for 12 years. More than 20,000 people have died in Turkey in the guerrilla war.

"Turkey is trying to enlarge its territory. We do not accept that," he said. "It is not the sole purpose of the Turks to fight against the PKK. They want to enlarge their boundaries and serve other political objectives as well."
The commander would not disclose the size of his band, but local villagers estimated the group at several hundred.
In March of 1995, 35,000 Turkish troops backed by armour and air power pushed 40 km (25 miles) into northern Iraq in pursuit of PKK fighters.
The troops smashed rebel camps and seized weapons and stores but encountered little real resistance, before pulling back in May. PKK rebels soon returned to their border bases.
